caveats: Requires a local KEX initiation from a non-IO thread (app-thread reExchangeKeys, switchToNoneCipher, or client startup racing early peer messages) concurrent with inbound peer KEXINIT.
Requires the peer to send a KEX message (e.g. first-kex-packet-follows guess per RFC 4253 s7.1, which the code anticipates) before our KEXINIT send completes.
subclaims.reason: doKexNegotiation CASes INIT->RUN (AbstractSession.java:891) but kex is only assigned later in performKexNegotiation (AbstractSession.java:948-949), fired by the initFuture listener (AbstractSession.java:918-928) which completes in sendKexInit (AbstractSession.java:2735). If a user thread CASes DONE->INIT via reExchangeKeys/requestNewKeysExchange (AbstractSession.java:2525-2591) while the IO thread concurrently processes peer KEXINIT (AbstractSession.java:872-877), the IO thread registers a pending listener and returns, leaving state RUN with kex null. The decode loop then processes a pipelined peer KEX message in the same thread (AbstractSession.java:1738); such guessed first packets are expected (AbstractSession.java:621-631). handleKexMessage only validates state RUN (AbstractSession.java:768) and dereferences kex at AbstractSession.java:771, so it throws NullPointerException. No common lock guards this: kex is a plain field (AbstractSession.java:163) and the RUN check does not test for null.
